## Learning Outcomes {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## 🎯 Learning Outcomes

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Apply** the four main cost estimation techniques including function point analysis
2. **Develop** a project budget and cost baseline (S-curve)
3. **Build** a bottom-up cost estimate using a WBS cost template
4. **Calculate** all core EVM metrics (PV, EV, AC, CPI, SPI, EAC, ETC, TCPI)
5. **Interpret** EVM status reports and forecast project outcomes
6. **Identify** cost control techniques and corrective actions
7. **Explain** contingency and management reserves
:::

## Cost Estimation

**Cost estimation** is the process of predicting the financial cost of completing project work.

### Estimation Classes (AACE International Standard)

| Class | Stage | Scope Definition | Accuracy | Usage |
|-------|-------|-----------------|----------|-------|
| **Class 5** | Concept | 0–2% | –50% to +100% | Screening, go/no-go |
| **Class 4** | Study | 1–15% | –30% to +50% | Feasibility |
| **Class 3** | Preliminary | 10–40% | –20% to +30% | Budget approval |
| **Class 2** | Detailed | 30–70% | –10% to +15% | Cost control |
| **Class 1** | Definitive | 50–100% | –5% to +5% | Tendering |

: AACE Cost Estimate Classes {.striped .hover}

### Estimation Techniques

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Analogous (Top-Down)
**Based on historical data from similar projects**

$$Cost_{new} = Cost_{historical} \times Adjustment\ Factor$$

*When to use:* Early project stages; limited detail available

**Cost Capacity Factor (Six-Tenths Rule):**
$$Cost_B = Cost_A \times \left(\frac{Capacity_B}{Capacity_A}\right)^{0.6}$$

*Example:* "Our last desalination plant (50 ML/day) cost $85M. This one is 65 ML/day:  
$85M × (65/50)^{0.6} = $85M × 1.21 ≈ **$103M**"

Accuracy: ±25% to ±50%

## Parametric
**Mathematical models based on units of measure**

*Examples:*
- Civil works: $450/m² × 3,500 m² = $1,575,000
- Earthworks: $28/m³ × 15,000 m³ = $420,000
- Electrical: $650/circuit × 180 circuits = $117,000

Accuracy: ±10% to ±25%

## Bottom-Up
**Estimate each work package individually, then sum**

Most accurate; most time-consuming.

*For each activity:*
1. Materials: Quantity × Unit rate
2. Labour: Hours × Hourly rate
3. Equipment: Hours/days × Hire rate
4. Overheads: (L + M + E) × OH%
5. Profit/margin (for contractors)

Accuracy: ±5% to ±15%

## Three-Point (PERT)
**Optimistic, Most Likely, Pessimistic applied to cost**

$$CE = \frac{O + 4M + P}{6}$$

Used to build **cost contingency** from risk analysis.

:::

## Bottom-Up Cost Estimate — Complete Example

The following **real-world cost estimate** follows the WBS structure for an IT/Engineering project. It demonstrates how a project manager builds a detailed Class 2 estimate.

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## 💡 Solved Example 7.1 — Bottom-Up WBS Cost Estimate

**Project:** Enterprise IT System Development  
**Estimate Class:** Class 2 (Detailed — 30–70% scope definition)

| WBS Item | Units/Hrs | Cost/Unit/Hr | Subtotals | WBS Level 1 Totals | % of Total |
|----------|-----------|-------------|-----------|---------------------|------------|
| **1. Project Management** | | | | **$306,300** | **20.1%** |
| 1.1 Project manager | 960 hrs | $100/hr | $96,000 | | |
| 1.2 Project team members | 1,920 hrs | $75/hr | $144,000 | | |
| Contractors (10% of software dev & testing) | | | $66,300 | | |
| **2. Hardware** | | | | **$76,000** | **5.0%** |
| 2.1 Handheld devices | 100 units | $600/unit | $60,000 | | |
| 2.2 Servers | 4 units | $4,000/unit | $16,000 | | |
| **3. Software** | | | | **$614,000** | **40.4%** |
| 3.1 Licensed software | 100 licences | $200/licence | $20,000 | | |
| 3.2 Software development* | — | — | $594,000 | | |
| **4. Testing** (10% of hardware + software) | | | | **$69,000** | **4.5%** |
| **5. Training & Support** | | | | **$202,400** | **13.3%** |
| 5.1 Trainee cost | 100 trainees | $500/trainee | $50,000 | | |
| 5.2 Travel cost | 12 trips | $700/trip | $8,400 | | |
| 5.3 Project team members | 1,920 hrs | $75/hr | $144,000 | | |
| **6. Reserves** (20% of base estimate) | | | | **$253,540** | **16.7%** |
| **TOTAL PROJECT COST ESTIMATE** | | | | **$1,521,240** | |

: WBS-Based Bottom-Up Cost Estimate {.striped .hover}

**Software Development Detail (Function Point Approach):**

| Component | Quantity | Conversion Factor | Function Points |
|-----------|----------|-------------------|-----------------|
| External inputs | 10 | 4 | 40 |
| External interface files | 3 | 7 | 21 |
| External outputs | 3 | 5 | 15 |
| External queries | 3 | 4 | 12 |
| Logical internal tables | 6 | 10 | 60 |
| **Total Function Points** | | | **148** |

- Java 2 language equivalency: 46 SLOC per function point
- Estimated SLOC: 148 × 46 = **6,808 lines of code**
- Productivity factor: 30.27 person-months
- Total labour hours: 4,843 hours at $120/hr
- **Total software development estimate: $581,106** (rounded to $594,000 with 2.2% contingency)
:::

## The Project Budget and Cost Baseline

The **cost baseline** (S-curve) shows planned cumulative expenditure over time.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Project budget structure: from estimates to reserves"
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'nodeSpacing': 30, 'rankSpacing': 60}}}%%
graph TD
    A["📋 Work Package Cost Estimates<br/>(Bottom-up per WBS work package)"]
    B["📊 Control Accounts<br/>(Sum of work packages)"]
    C["🗂️ Cost Baseline<br/>= Sum of Control Accounts + Contingency<br/>(Excludes Management Reserve)"]
    D["🔒 Management Reserve<br/>PM's buffer for unknown-unknowns<br/>(Sponsor controlled)"]
    E["💰 Budget at Completion (BAC)<br/>= Cost Baseline + Management Reserve"]

    A --> B --> C
    C --> E
    D --> E

    style E fill:#1d4ed8,color:#fff
    style C fill:#0f766e,color:#fff
    style D fill:#b91c1c,color:#fff
```

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## 📖 Contingency vs. Management Reserve

**Contingency Reserve:** For **known risks** (from the risk register). Controlled by the PM.

**Management Reserve:** For **unknown-unknowns**. Controlled by the Project Sponsor.

*Typical reserves:*
- Contingency: 5–15% of base estimate
- Management Reserve: 5–10% of base estimate
:::

## Earned Value Management (EVM)

**Earned Value Management (EVM)** integrates scope, schedule, and cost into a single measurement system — giving you an objective view of project status at any point.

### The Three Core EVM Values

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## 📖 The Three Fundamental EVM Metrics

| Metric | Acronym | Old Name | Question it Answers |
|--------|---------|----------|---------------------|
| **Planned Value** | PV | BCWS | How much work was *planned* to be done (in $)? |
| **Earned Value** | EV | BCWP | How much work has actually been *accomplished* (in $)? |
| **Actual Cost** | AC | ACWP | How much have we actually *spent* (in $)? |
:::

### EVM Formulas Reference Card

| Metric | Formula | Positive = Good | Negative = Bad |
|--------|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| **SV** (Schedule Variance) | $EV - PV$ | Ahead of schedule | Behind schedule |
| **CV** (Cost Variance) | $EV - AC$ | Under budget | Over budget |
| **SPI** (Schedule Performance Index) | $EV / PV$ | > 1 = ahead | < 1 = behind |
| **CPI** (Cost Performance Index) | $EV / AC$ | > 1 = under budget | < 1 = over budget |
| **EAC** (Estimate at Completion) | $BAC / CPI$ | — | — |
| **ETC** (Estimate to Complete) | $EAC - AC$ | — | — |
| **VAC** (Variance at Completion) | $BAC - EAC$ | Positive = under budget | Negative = over budget |
| **TCPI** (To-Complete Perf. Index) | $(BAC - EV) / (BAC - AC)$ | < 1 = easy | > 1 = needs improvement |

: EVM Formulas Quick Reference {.striped .hover}

---

## Complete EVM Solved Example — Real Project Data

The following complete example is based on **real earned value data** from a software project tracked over its full 12-month life cycle.

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## 💡 Solved Example 7.2 — Full EVM Walk-Through

**Project:** Database Management System — **Budget at Completion (BAC) = $100,000**  
**Duration:** 12 months (January–December)  
**Status Date:** End of May (Month 5)

**Step 1: Monthly Planned Value (PV) per activity**

The Planned Value for each activity is the approved budget for work *scheduled* to be done:

| Activity | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun | Jul | Aug | Sep | Oct | Nov | Dec | **Total PV** |
|----------|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-------------|
| Plan & Staff Project | $4,000 | $4,000 | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | $8,000 |
| Analyse Requirements | — | $6,000 | $6,000 | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | $12,000 |
| Develop ERDs | — | — | $4,000 | $4,000 | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | $8,000 |
| Design DB Tables | — | — | — | $6,000 | $4,000 | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | $10,000 |
| Design Forms/Reports | — | — | — | — | $8,000 | $4,000 | — | — | — | — | — | — | $8,000* |
| Construct Prototype | — | — | — | — | — | $10,000 | — | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| Test/Eval Prototype | — | — | — | — | — | $2,000 | $6,000 | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| User Feedback | — | — | — | — | — | — | $4,000 | $6,000 | $4,000 | — | — | — | — |
| Test System | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | $4,000 | $4,000 | $2,000 | — | — |
| Document System | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | $3,000 | $1,000 | — |
| **Monthly PV** | **$4,000** | **$10,000** | **$10,000** | **$10,000** | **$12,000** | **$16,000** | **$10,000** | **$6,000** | **$8,000** | **$4,000** | **$5,000** | **$5,000** | — |
| **Cumulative PV** | $4,000 | $14,000 | $24,000 | $34,000 | **$46,000** | $62,000 | $72,000 | $78,000 | $86,000 | $90,000 | $95,000 | $100,000 | |

*\*Design Forms/Reports is only 75% planned complete by May*

**Step 2: Earned Value (EV) — actual work accomplished**

EV = Budgeted Cost × Actual % Complete

| Activity | Total PV | Planned % | Actual % | EV ($) | Notes |
|----------|---------|-----------|----------|--------|-------|
| Plan & Staff Project | $8,000 | 100% | **100%** | $8,000 | Complete ✅ |
| Analyse Requirements | $12,000 | 100% | **100%** | $12,000 | Complete ✅ |
| Develop ERDs | $8,000 | 100% | **100%** | $8,000 | Complete ✅ |
| Design DB Tables | $10,000 | 100% | **100%** | $10,000 | Complete ✅ |
| Design Forms/Reports | $8,000 | 75% | **50%** | **$5,333** | Only 50% done (behind!) |
| Construct Prototype | — | 0% | 0% | $0 | Not started |
| Test/Eval Prototype | — | 0% | 0% | $0 | Not started |
| **TOTAL EV at May 31** | | | | **$43,333** | |

**Step 3: Actual Cost (AC) at May 31**

| Month | Monthly AC | Cumulative AC |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| January | $4,000 | $4,000 |
| February | $11,000 | $15,000 |
| March | $11,000 | $26,000 |
| April | $12,000 | $38,000 |
| May | $15,000 | **$53,000** |

**Step 4: Calculate All EVM Metrics**

| Metric | Formula | Calculation | Result | Interpretation |
|--------|---------|------------|--------|----------------|
| **PV** | Planned | — | **$46,000** | Budgeted work planned by May 31 |
| **EV** | Earned | — | **$43,333** | Value of work actually done |
| **AC** | Actual | — | **$53,000** | Money actually spent |
| **SV** | EV − PV | 43,333 − 46,000 | **−$2,667** | ⚠️ $2,667 behind schedule |
| **CV** | EV − AC | 43,333 − 53,000 | **−$9,667** | 🚨 $9,667 over budget |
| **SPI** | EV/PV | 43,333/46,000 | **0.942** | Doing 94.2% of planned work |
| **CPI** | EV/AC | 43,333/53,000 | **0.818** | Getting $0.82 value per $1 spent |
| **EAC** | BAC/CPI | 100,000/0.818 | **$122,308** | Forecast final cost |
| **ETC** | EAC − AC | 122,308 − 53,000 | **$69,308** | Still need $69K more to finish |
| **VAC** | BAC − EAC | 100,000 − 122,308 | **−$22,308** | Expected overrun of $22,308 |
| **TCPI** | (BAC−EV)/(BAC−AC) | (100K−43,333)/(100K−53K) | **1.206** | Need 20.6% better cost efficiency! |

: Full EVM Status Table at May 31 {.striped .hover}

**Step 5: S-Curve and EVM Chart**

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "EVM S-Curve showing PV, EV, AC and forecast through project completion"
xychart-beta
    title "EVM S-Curve — Database Project ($000)"
    x-axis ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May ◄NOW", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]
    y-axis "Cumulative Cost ($000)" 0 --> 125
    line [4, 14, 24, 34, 46, 62, 72, 78, 86, 90, 95, 100]
    line [4, 14, 24, 34, 43, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    line [4, 15, 26, 38, 53, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
```

*Blue line = PV (planned); Orange line = EV (earned); Red line = AC (actual)*

**Step 6: Status Narrative**

> **Project Status Report — May 31**
>
> As of the end of May, the database project is **behind schedule (SPI = 0.94)** and **over budget (CPI = 0.82)**. The primary driver of poor cost performance is the "Design Forms, Reports & Queries" activity, which is only 50% complete against a planned 75%, while costs have continued at the budgeted rate. If current cost performance continues, the project is forecast to complete at **$122,308** — a **$22,308 (22.3%) overrun** against the approved budget of $100,000. Recommended actions: (1) Re-estimate remaining work on Forms/Reports activity; (2) Identify specific root causes of cost overrun in April and May; (3) Present options to sponsor: scope reduction, budget increase, or schedule extension.

**TCPI Warning:** A TCPI of 1.206 means the team must achieve 20.6% better cost efficiency on all remaining work than it has achieved to date. This is generally considered unrealistic without significant interventions.
:::

## EVM Status Interpretation Guide

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "EVM status quadrant — interpreting CPI and SPI together"
quadrantChart
    title EVM Status Quadrant (CPI vs SPI)
    x-axis "Over Budget (CPI < 1)" --> "Under Budget (CPI > 1)"
    y-axis "Behind Schedule (SPI < 1)" --> "Ahead of Schedule (SPI > 1)"
    quadrant-1 "✅ BEST CASE<br/>Ahead + Under Budget"
    quadrant-2 "⚠️ CHECK SCOPE<br/>Ahead but Over Budget"
    quadrant-3 "🚨 CRITICAL<br/>Behind + Over Budget"
    quadrant-4 "⚠️ AT RISK<br/>Behind but Under Budget"
    Our Project: [0.3, 0.42]
    Ideal: [0.85, 0.85]
    Warning Zone: [0.35, 0.35]
```

| CPI / SPI | Condition | Action Required |
|-----------|-----------|----------------|
| Both ≥ 1.0 | On or under budget, on or ahead of schedule | Continue; investigate if >1.2 (too optimistic?) |
| CPI < 1 only | Over budget, but on schedule | Investigate labour productivity; check estimates |
| SPI < 1 only | Behind schedule, but on budget | Investigate activity constraints; consider crashing |
| Both < 1.0 | **Critical — behind AND over budget** | Immediate corrective action; escalate to sponsor |
| CPI < 0.85 | **Severe cost overrun** | Executive intervention required |

: EVM Response Matrix {.striped .hover}

## Cost Control

Cost control involves **monitoring, forecasting, and taking corrective action**:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Cost control cycle"
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'nodeSpacing': 30, 'rankSpacing': 60}}}%%
flowchart LR
    M["📊 MEASURE<br/>Collect actual costs<br/>Calculate EV from work done"] --> A
    A["📈 ANALYSE<br/>Calculate CV & CPI<br/>Forecast EAC"] --> R
    R{"Performance
acceptable?"}
    R --> |"Yes"| CO["✅ Continue<br/>Monitor next period"]
    R --> |"No"| CA["⚠️ Corrective Action<br/>Identify root cause<br/>Develop & approve plan"]
    CA --> U["📋 UPDATE<br/>Revised estimate<br/>Change request & report"]
    U --> M
    CO --> M

    style M fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#3b82f6
    style A fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#eab308
    style CA fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#ef4444
    style CO fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#22c55e
```

### Cost Control Techniques

::: {.panel-tabset}

## EVM Trending
Monitor CPI and SPI trends weekly:
- Is CPI improving or deteriorating?
- Historical research shows: **CPI rarely improves by more than 10%** from its value at 20% project completion
- Early warning: CPI < 0.9 at 20% completion = high overrun risk

## Cost Forecasting
Review EAC regularly and communicate honestly:
- **EAC = BAC/CPI** — if current cost performance continues (most common)
- **EAC = AC + (BAC−EV)** — if remaining work will be done at original budget
- **EAC = AC + ETC** — if an independent re-estimate of remaining work is done

Compare all three forecasts monthly — divergence signals problems.

## Change Control
All cost changes must go through formal change control:
1. Identify cost trending beyond threshold (typically ±5%)
2. Issue early warning notice to client
3. Raise formal change request
4. Get written approval before spending additional funds

## Recovery Strategies
When the project is over budget:
1. **Value Engineering** — achieve same outcome at lower cost
2. **Scope reduction** — formally remove lower-priority deliverables
3. **Productivity improvement** — identify and remove bottlenecks
4. **Procurement re-negotiation** — re-tender over-budget packages
5. **Request Management Reserve** — request release from sponsor

:::

## Case Study — Riyadh Metro: Cost Management at Arab Mega-Scale {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## 🏭 Case Study: Riyadh Metro — Managing a $22.5 Billion Urban Rail Programme

**Background:**  
The Riyadh Metro (مترو الرياض) — **6 lines, 176 km, 85 stations** — was built concurrently in a single city from 2013 to 2021. It is the largest single transport programme in the Arab world.

**Project Financials:**

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Approved Budget | $22.5 billion USD |
| Final Actual Cost | ~$23–24 billion |
| Cost Variance | +4–7% (exceptional for this scale) |
| Contract Structure | 5 mega-contracts, each > $3 billion |

**Cost Management Innovations:**

| Innovation | Description | Result |
|------------|-------------|--------|
| Programme-level EVM | Single EVM template for all 5 consortia | Cross-contract cost visibility |
| GMP with gain-share | Contractor gets 50% of savings below GMP; absorbs 70% of overruns | Aligned contractor incentives |
| Independent ISCA | Third-party review of all claims before payment | Eliminated inflated progress claims |
| Real-time cost dashboard | Accessible to ADA, Ministry of Finance, and all PMs | Line 4 (CPI=0.87 at 35%) triggered intervention 18 months before crisis |

**EVM Alert Example:**

> *Line 4 showed CPI = 0.87 at 35% complete (early 2016). An ADA intervention team was on site within two weeks — well before the cost variance became a payment crisis.*

**Discussion Questions:**
1. Why might a GMP contract be more appropriate for complex metro construction than fixed-price lump sum?
2. If Line 3 is at CPI = 0.91 with 45% complete (BAC = $4.2 billion), calculate the EAC.
3. How does independent cost auditing reduce the principal-agent problem in mega-project procurement?

*Sources: @ada2021metro; @riyadh2020pmo*
:::

## ✏️ Exercise 7.1 — Cost Estimation

You are estimating the cost of a **new wastewater treatment plant** (5 ML/day capacity).

**Part A — Analogous Estimate:**
- A 3 ML/day plant was built 3 years ago for $4.2 million
- Construction price index has increased by 12% over 3 years
- Cost capacity factor for treatment plants: 0.65

1. Estimate the current cost of the 5 ML/day plant

**Part B — Bottom-Up Parametric:**

| Work Package | Quantity | Unit Rate |
|-------------|---------|---------|
| Civil earthworks | 8,500 m³ | $28/m³ |
| Reinforced concrete structures | 420 m³ | $1,850/m³ |
| Mechanical equipment | 1 lump sum | $650,000 |
| Pipework and fittings | 280 m | $450/m |
| Electrical and instrumentation | 1 lump sum | $380,000 |
| Building and site works | 350 m² | $2,100/m² |

Add 12% overhead, 8% contingency, and 5% management reserve.

**Part C — Compare:** Why might your two estimates differ?
:::

::: {.callout-caution icon="false"}

## 🖥️ MS Project Practice — Cost & Earned Value {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## Microsoft Project: Applying Chapter 7 Concepts

With resources and rates assigned in your project file, MS Project can calculate and track costs automatically:

**Tasks to complete in MS Project:**

1. **Verify resource rates** are entered correctly in the Resource Sheet (Std. Rate, Ovt. Rate, Cost/Use, Accrue At = Prorated for most resources)
2. **Add fixed costs**: In Gantt Chart view, right-click a column header → Insert Column → Fixed Cost. Enter any fixed procurement or subcontract costs directly against the relevant task
3. **View the Cost table**: View → Table → Cost. This shows Baseline Cost, Actual Cost, Remaining Cost, and Cost Variance for every task
4. **Check the project total cost**: Project tab → Project Information → Statistics button. Verify the total cost matches your bottom-up estimate
5. **Set the cost baseline** (if not already done): Project → Set Baseline → this freezes Baseline Cost values
6. **Enter progress for 3–4 weeks** of your project (% Complete per task using actual data or the exercise data from Chapter 6 Exercise 6.3)
7. **Generate the Earned Value report**: Report tab → Costs → Earned Value Report. Read off:
   - **PV** (Planned Value / BCWS) — shown as "Baseline Cost" at the status date
   - **EV** (Earned Value / BCWP) — shown as "Earned Value"
   - **AC** (Actual Cost / ACWP) — shown as "Actual Cost"
   - **CPI** and **SPI** — calculated automatically
   - **EAC** (Estimate at Completion) — MS Project uses EAC = BAC / CPI by default
8. **Set the Status Date**: Project tab → Project Information → Status Date. MS Project uses this date when calculating EV metrics — set it to the end of your last reported week
9. **View the Tracking Gantt** and identify tasks where Cost Variance (CV) is negative (over budget). What corrective actions would you recommend?

**Expected outcome:** Your MS Project EV figures should match the manual EVM calculations from the Chapter 7 exercises. Differences of more than 5% indicate a data entry error — check actual start dates and % complete values.
:::
